name: Yonggwang (Hanbit) Reactor Neutrino Site

operator.note: No source fetched this session states an operator of the RENO experimental site distinct from the RENO collaboration and the adjacent Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant (operated by KHNP, not itself fetched this session).

intervals.label: hosting RENO
intervals.quote: In the 229 day data-taking period between 11 August 2011 and 26 March 2012
intervals.note: No official facility page was reachable this session to independently source a facility-level founding/operating interval; start is RENO's own data-taking start date. `end` left null (ongoing at `verified_at`, §2.3) since no source confirms a shutdown.

notes: RENO's own official site domain guessed this session (reno.snu.ac.kr, home.kias.re.kr/MKG/h/reno) failed DNS/connection; this record relies on the 2012 arXiv discovery paper, INSPIRE, and the Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant's Wikipedia page (used only for an approximate regional coordinate).

summary.plain: The site near the Hanbit (formerly Yonggwang) nuclear power plant in South Korea where the RENO experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from six reactors.
summary.technical: Reactor-neutrino site at the Hanbit (Yonggwang) Nuclear Power Plant, South Korea, hosting the RENO near (294 m) and far (1383 m) detector halls, 6 x 2.8 GW_th reactor array.
